name: b10c
cooked:
b10c:

yes, there’s a long tail. Maybe it makes sense to expand it to more ISPs. Maybe I can automate that somehow - doing it manually was very time consuming. I see that the ipinfo.io API offers a “type” field, but that’s only returned in the paid version, which I don’t have access too. Surely there are alternatives..

I went ahead and fetched the ASN classification from the ipinfo.io website… Using all ASN classified as “isp” yields the following plots for the Bitnodes and KIT data. Since they are different data sources and the IP->ASN method is different for them (For Bitnodes we use ASMAP, KIT DSN data has an ASN field), they have a different number of ISPs.

Using Bitnodes data:

Change in residential node count since Bitcoin Core v30.0 release (1410 residential ASNs; bitnodes data)1390×690 83.5 KB

Bitnodes data suggests +200-250 residential nodes since v30.0 release at the moment.

Using KIT DSN data:

Change in residential node count since Bitcoin Core v30.0 release (1311 residential ASNs; KIT DSN data)1390×690 94.3 KB

KIT DSN data suggests +150-200 residential nodes since v30.0 release at the moment.
